doc: The same kernel on FLOAT64 coordinates (cells of both signs up to +-300): every intermediate stays float64 and the result is float64, so a float64 port is checked tightly. It differs from the float32 evaluation of the same points by up to 1.2e-6 (see perlin3.f32.random). Closed form: rtol 1e-9, atol 1e-12. The permutation input plan<i>.perm is the draw as recorded (256 entries for Perlin3, 1024 for Worley3); the kernel indexes it DOUBLED, concat(perm, perm) (512 or 2048 entries, so p[i + 256] = p[i]): a port that indexes the stored array directly runs off its end (see the .table cases).
